tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Extension of a Tangent Vector to a Global Vector Field]

↗ prop:existence-partitions-unity

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $p \in M$, and let $v \in T_pM$. Then there is a smooth vector field $Z \in \mathfrak {X}(M)$ with $Z_p = v$.

Proof

For each $x \in M$ let $t_x \subseteq T_xM$ be the singleton $\{ v\} $ if $x = p$, and all of $T_xM$ otherwise. Each $t_x$ is convex, being either a one-point set or a vector space. We claim every point of $M$ has a neighbourhood carrying a smooth local vector field whose value at each $x$ lies in $t_x$.

Near $p$: choose a local trivialization $\Phi $ of $TM$ over a neighbourhood $U$ of $p$, and let $c$ be the fibre coordinate of $v$, so that $\Phi (v) = (p, c)$. The local field $x \mapsto \Phi ^{-1}(x, c)$ is smooth on $U$, being constant in the trivialization, and its value at $p$ is $v$; so its value lies in $t_x$ for every $x \in U$, the constraint being vacuous away from $p$.

Near any $q \neq p$: the zero section is smooth on the neighbourhood $M \setminus \{ p\} $ of $q$, and its value lies in $t_x = T_xM$ for every $x$ there.

Now let $\{ \psi _\alpha \} $ be a smooth partition of unity subordinate to the cover by these neighbourhoods (Proposition 4), let $Z_\alpha $ be the local field carried by the $\alpha $-th neighbourhood, and set $Z = \sum _\alpha \psi _\alpha Z_\alpha $, a smooth global vector field. At each $x \in M$, $Z_x$ is a convex combination of elements of $t_x$, hence lies in $t_x$ by convexity. In particular $Z_p \in t_p = \{ v\} $, that is, $Z_p = v$.

□
